summary: A witness for the new moon must be someone the Beis Din knows. After some people sent false witnesses, the Sages made a rule to accept only witnesses they know.

chunks.en: If the Beis Din does not know him,
chunks.st: If the members of the Great Sanhedrin in Jerusalem are not familiar with that
chunks.stMore: one who saw the new moon, i.e., that he is a valid witness, the members of his local court of twenty-three

chunks.en: his town sends another person with him to say he is a good witness.
chunks.st: send another with him to testify about him.

chunks.en: At first, they would accept witnesses
chunks.st: The mishna adds: Initially, the court would accept testimony to determine the start

chunks.en: about the new moon from any person.
chunks.st: of the month from any person,
chunks.stMore: as all are presumed to be qualified witnesses, absent any disqualifying factors.

chunks.en: When the minim spoiled it,
chunks.explain: They sent false witnesses on purpose.
chunks.st: However, when the Boethusians, a sect whose members had their own opinions with regard to the establishment of the Festivals, corrupted
chunks.stMore: the process by sending false witnesses to testify about the new moon,

words.note: The Baisusim, a group who did not follow the Sages.

chunks.en: the Sages made a rule that they would accept witnesses
chunks.st: the Sages instituted that they would accept this testimony

chunks.en: only from people they know.
chunks.st: only from those men familiar to the Sanhedrin as valid witnesses.

summary: At first, the news of Rosh Chodesh was spread by lighting fires on mountaintops. When the Kusim tricked people with false fires, messengers were sent instead.

chunks.en: At first, they would light torches.
chunks.explain: On mountaintops, to show far away that it was Rosh Chodesh.
chunks.st: Initially, after the court sanctified the new month they would light torches
chunks.stMore: on the mountaintops, from one peak to another, to signal to the community in Babylonia that the month had been sanctified.

chunks.en: When the Kusim spoiled it,
chunks.explain: They lit torches at the wrong times to confuse people.
chunks.st: After the Samaritans [Kutim] corrupted
chunks.stMore: and ruined this method by lighting torches at the wrong times to confuse the Jews,

words.note: Samaritans, a people who lived in Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: the Sages made a rule that messengers should go out.
chunks.st: the Sages instituted that messengers should go out
chunks.stMore: to the Diaspora and inform them of the start of the month.

summary: How did they send the message with torches? They lit a torch on a mountain and waved it until they saw the next mountain wave a torch too.

chunks.en: How would they light the torches?
chunks.st: The mishna asks: How would they light the torches during that earlier period?

chunks.en: They brought long poles of cedar wood,
chunks.st: They would bring items that burn well, e.g., long poles of cedar,

chunks.en: and reeds, and pine wood, and threads of
chunks.st: reeds, pinewood, and beaten

chunks.en: flax, and he tied them with a string.
chunks.st: flax, and tie them together with a string.

chunks.en: And he went up to the top of the mountain and lit
chunks.st: And someone would then ascend to the top of the mountain and light

chunks.en: a fire with them.
chunks.st: the torch on fire with them,

chunks.en: And he waved it back and forth, and up and down,
chunks.st: and wave it back and forth and up and down,

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁהוּא רוֹאֶה אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ שֶׁהוּא
chunks.en: until he saw his friend
chunks.st: until he would see his colleague

chunks.en: doing the same on top of the second mountain.
chunks.st: doing likewise on the top of the second mountain.
chunks.stMore: In this manner he would know that the next messenger had received the message and passed it on.

chunks.en: And so on the top of the third mountain.
chunks.st: And similarly, the second torchbearer would wait for a signal from the one on the top of the third mountain,
chunks.stMore: and so on. In this manner the message would reach the Diaspora.

summary: This mishnah names the mountains where the torches were lit, from Yerushalayim all the way until the whole golah was lit up like one big fire.

chunks.en: And from where did they light the torches?
chunks.st: And from which mountains would they light the torches?

chunks.en: From Har HaMishchah to Sartava,
chunks.st: They would transmit the message from the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem to Sartava,

words.note: Har HaZeisim, the Mount of Olives, by Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: and from Sartava to Grofina,
chunks.st: and from Sartava to Gerofina,

chunks.en: and from Grofina to Chavran,
chunks.st: and from Gerofina to Ḥavran,

chunks.en: and from Chavran to Beis Biltin.
chunks.st: and from Ḥavran to Beit Baltin.

chunks.en: And from Beis Biltin they did not move on to another place.
chunks.st: And from Beit Baltin they would not move
chunks.stMore: to light torches in any other predetermined location.

chunks.en: Instead, he waved the torch back and forth, and up and down,
chunks.st: Rather, the one who was appointed for this task would wave the torch back and forth and up and down,

chunks.en: until he saw the whole golah
chunks.st: until he would see the entire Diaspora

words.note: The Jews living outside Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: lit up before him like one big bonfire.
chunks.st: before him alight like one large bonfire,
chunks.stMore: as they would light torches to continue transmitting the message from place to place all the way to the farthest reaches of the Diaspora.

summary: Witnesses for the new moon gathered in a big courtyard in Yerushalayim and were treated well. Rabban Gamliel the Elder let them walk two thousand amos on Shabbos, and also others who come to help.

chunks.en: There was a big courtyard in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: There was a large courtyard in Jerusalem,

chunks.en: and it was called Beis Yaazek.
chunks.st: which was called Beit Ya’zek.

chunks.en: All the witnesses gathered there,
chunks.st: And there all the witnesses coming to testify about the new moon would gather,

chunks.en: and the Beis Din checked them there.
chunks.st: and the court of seventy-one judges would examine them there.

chunks.en: And they made big meals for them,
chunks.st: And they would prepare great feasts for them,

chunks.en: so that they would be happy to come again.
chunks.st: so that they would be willing and accustomed to coming and submitting their testimony.

chunks.en: At first, they would not move
chunks.st: Initially, when witnesses would arrive on Shabbat from a distant place, they would not move

chunks.en: from there the whole day.
chunks.explain: On Shabbos, they had walked past the Shabbos limit to get there.
chunks.st: from there all day,
chunks.stMore: as they had left their Shabbat limit, and it was consequently prohibited for them to walk more than four cubits in any direction once they had completed their mission. Concerned that this limitation would discourage witnesses from coming,

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel the Elder made a rule that they may
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted that the witnesses be permitted to

chunks.en: walk two thousand amos in every direction.
chunks.st: walk two thousand cubits in each direction. The mishna continues:

words.note: An amah is about the length of an arm.

chunks.en: And not only these people,
chunks.st: And not only these
chunks.stMore: witnesses are granted two thousand cubits from their new place,

chunks.en: but also a midwife who comes to help a baby be born,
chunks.st: but this applies also to a midwife who comes to deliver a child,

words.note: A woman who helps when a baby is born.

chunks.en: and someone who comes to save people from a fire, or from
chunks.st: and one who comes to rescue Jews from a fire, from

chunks.en: an army, or from a river, or from a falling building.
chunks.st: an invasion of gentile troops, from a flooding river, or from the collapse of a building.

chunks.en: These are like the people of the city,
chunks.st: All these are considered like the inhabitants of the city where they arrive,

chunks.he: וְיֵשׁ לָהֶם אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכָל רוּחַ:
chunks.en: and they may walk two thousand amos in every direction.
chunks.st: and therefore they have two thousand cubits in each direction.

summary: The Beis Din checked the witnesses one at a time, asking exactly how and where they saw the moon. If both witnesses' answers matched, their testimony was accepted.

chunks.en: How do they check the witnesses?
chunks.st: How do they examine the witnesses who come to testify about the new moon?

chunks.en: The pair that came first,
chunks.st: They deal with them in order, as the pair of witnesses that arrives first

chunks.en: they check first.
chunks.st: they examine first.

chunks.he: וּמַכְנִיסִין אֶת הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבָּהֶן וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ,
chunks.en: They bring in the older one and say to him,
chunks.st: They bring in the greater of the two witnesses, and they say to him:

chunks.en: "Tell us, how did you see the moon?
chunks.st: Say how you saw the moon.

chunks.en: In front of the sun, or behind the sun?
chunks.st: Was it in front of the sun or behind the sun?

chunks.en: To its north or to its south?
chunks.st: To its north or to its south?

chunks.he: כַּמָּה הָיָה גָבוֹהַּ וּלְאַיִן הָיָה נוֹטֶה,
chunks.en: How high was it, and which way was it leaning?
chunks.st: How high was the moon over the horizon, and in which direction did it tilt?

chunks.en: And how wide was it?"
chunks.st: And how wide was it?

chunks.en: If he said, "In front of the sun,"
chunks.st: If, for example, he said that he saw the moon in front of the sun,

chunks.en: he has said nothing.
chunks.explain: That cannot happen, so he must be wrong.
chunks.st: he has not said anything
chunks.stMore: of substance, as this is impossible and therefore he is either mistaken or lying.

chunks.en: And after that they would bring in
chunks.st: And after they finish hearing the first witness’s testimony, they would bring in

chunks.en: the second one and check him.
chunks.st: the second witness and examine him in a similar manner.

chunks.en: If their words match,
chunks.st: If their statements match,

chunks.en: their testimony stands.
chunks.st: their testimony is accepted and the court sanctifies the New Moon.

chunks.en: And all the other pairs, they ask
chunks.st: And the court then asks all the other pairs of witnesses

chunks.en: them just the main questions.
chunks.st: certain general matters, without probing into all the details.

chunks.en: Not because they need them,
chunks.st: They do this not because they require the additional testimony,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יֵצְאוּ בְּפַחֵי נֶפֶשׁ,
chunks.en: but so that they will not go away disappointed,
chunks.st: but so that the witnesses should not leave disappointed,

chunks.en: so that they will be happy to come again.
chunks.st: and so that the witnesses should be accustomed to coming
chunks.stMore: to testify, and will not hesitate to come the next time, when they might be needed.

summary: After the witnesses are accepted, the head of the Beis Din declares the new month holy and everyone answers. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says that if the moon was not seen on time, they do not declare it.

chunks.en: The head of the Beis Din says, "It is made holy!"
chunks.st: After the witnesses have been examined and their testimony accepted, the head of the court says: It is sanctified.

chunks.he: וְכָל הָעָם עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו מְקֻדָּשׁ מְקֻדָּשׁ.
chunks.en: And all the people answer after him, "It is made holy! It is made holy!"
chunks.st: And all the people respond after him: It is sanctified; it is sanctified.

chunks.en: Whether it was seen at its time,
chunks.st: Whether the moon was seen at its anticipated time, on the thirtieth day of the previous month,

chunks.en: or it was not seen at its time,
chunks.st: or whether it was not seen at its anticipated time,
chunks.stMore: in which case witnesses are not necessary to establish the following day as the New Moon,

chunks.en: they declare it holy.
chunks.st: the court sanctifies it
chunks.stMore: and formally proclaims the day as the New Moon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:

chunks.en: If it was not seen at its time,
chunks.st: If the new moon was not seen at its anticipated time,

chunks.en: they do not declare it holy,
chunks.st: the court does not sanctify the New Moon on the following day,

chunks.en: because Heaven already made it holy.
chunks.st: as the celestial court in Heaven has already sanctified it,
chunks.stMore: precluding the need for the additional sanctification by the earthly court.

summary: Rabban Gamliel used pictures of the moon to check witnesses. This mishnah tells of witnesses he accepted, though other Rabbis said they were not telling the truth.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel had pictures of the shapes of the moon
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel had a diagram of the different forms of the moon drawn

chunks.en: on a board on the wall of his upstairs room.
chunks.st: on a tablet that hung on the wall of his attic,

chunks.en: He would show them to simple people and say,
chunks.st: which he would show to the laymen who came to testify about the new moon but were unable to describe adequately what they had seen. And he would say to them:

chunks.en: "Did you see it like this, or like this?"
chunks.st: Did you see a form like this or like this?

chunks.en: Once, two witnesses came and said,
chunks.st: There was an incident in which two witnesses came to testify about the new moon, and they said:

chunks.en: "We saw it in the morning in the east, and in the evening in the west."
chunks.st: We saw the waning moon in the morning in the east, and that same day we saw the new moon in the evening in the west.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said:

chunks.en: "They are lying witnesses."
chunks.st: They are false witnesses,
chunks.stMore: as it is impossible to see the new moon so soon after the last sighting of the waning moon.

chunks.en: When they came to Yavneh, Rabban Gamliel accepted them.
chunks.st: However, when they arrived in Yavne, Rabban Gamliel accepted them as witnesses without concern.

chunks.en: Another time, two came and said,
chunks.st: And there was another incident in which two witnesses came and said:

chunks.en: "We saw it at its time,
chunks.st: We saw the new moon at its anticipated time,
chunks.stMore: i.e., on the night of the thirtieth day of the previous month;

chunks.en: but on the next night it was not seen."
chunks.st: however, on the following night, i.e., the start of the thirty-first, which is often the determinant of a full, thirty-day month, it was not seen.

chunks.en: And Rabban Gamliel accepted them.
chunks.st: And nevertheless Rabban Gamliel accepted their
chunks.stMore: testimony and established the New Moon on the thirtieth day.

chunks.en: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Dosa ben Horkinas disagreed and said:

chunks.en: "They are lying witnesses.
chunks.st: They are false witnesses;

chunks.en: How can people say that a woman had a baby,
chunks.st: how can witnesses testify that a woman gave birth

chunks.en: and the next day she is still waiting for it?"
chunks.explain: The moon cannot be seen one night and missing the next.
chunks.st: and the next day her belly is between her teeth,
chunks.stMore: i.e., she is obviously still pregnant? If the new moon was already visible at its anticipated time, how could it not be seen a day later?

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

chunks.en: "I agree with what you say."
chunks.st: I see the logic of your statement; the New Moon must be established a day later.

summary: Rabban Gamliel ordered Rabbi Yehoshua to come to him on the day Rabbi Yehoshua thought was Yom Kippur. Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Dosa showed him that we must follow the Beis Din, so he came, and Rabban Gamliel honored him.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel sent a message to Rabbi Yehoshua:
chunks.st: Upon hearing that Rabbi Yehoshua had challenged his ruling, Rabban Gamliel sent a message to him:

chunks.he: גּוֹזְרַנִי עָלֶיךָ שֶׁתָּבֹא אֶצְלִי בְּמַקֶּלְךָ וּבִמְעוֹתֶיךָ
chunks.en: "I order you to come to me with your stick and your money
chunks.st: I decree against you that you must appear before me with your staff and with your money

chunks.en: on the day that is Yom Kippur by your counting."
chunks.explain: By Rabban Gamliel's counting, it was the day after Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: on the day on which Yom Kippur occurs according to your calculation;
chunks.stMore: according to my calculation, that day is the eleventh of Tishrei, the day after Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva went and found him upset.
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva went and found Rabbi Yehoshua distressed
chunks.stMore: that the head of the Great Sanhedrin was forcing him to desecrate the day that he maintained was Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: In an attempt to console him, Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.en: "I can learn that everything
chunks.st: I can learn from a verse that everything that

chunks.en: that Rabban Gamliel did counts,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel did in sanctifying the month is done, i.e., it is valid.

chunks.en: as it says in Vayikra,
chunks.st: As it is stated:

chunks.en: 'These are the Yamim Tovim of Hashem, holy gatherings,
chunks.st: “These are the appointed seasons of the Lord, sacred convocations,

chunks.en: which you shall call.'
chunks.st: which you shall proclaim in their season” (Leviticus 23:4).

chunks.en: Whether they are set at the right time or not at the right time,
chunks.st: This verse indicates that whether you have proclaimed them at their proper time or whether you have declared them not at their proper time,

chunks.en: these are the only Yamim Tovim I have."
chunks.st: I have only these Festivals
chunks.stMore: as established by the representatives of the Jewish people.

chunks.en: Then he came to Rabbi
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua then came to Rabbi

chunks.en: Dosa ben Harkinas.
chunks.st: Dosa ben Horkinas,

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: who said to him:

chunks.en: "If we come to question
chunks.st: If we come to debate and question the rulings of

chunks.en: the Beis Din of Rabban Gamliel,
chunks.st: the court of Rabban Gamliel,

chunks.en: we must question every
chunks.st: we must debate and question the rulings of every

chunks.en: Beis Din that has stood
chunks.st: court that has stood

chunks.en: from the days of Moshe until now.
chunks.st: from the days of Moses until now.

chunks.en: As it says in Shemos,
chunks.st: As it is stated:

chunks.en: 'Then Moshe went up, and Aharon, Nadav
chunks.st: “Then Moses went up, and Aaron, Nadav

chunks.en: and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisrael.'
chunks.st: and Avihu, and seventy of the Elders of Israel” (Exodus 24:9).

chunks.he: וְלָמָּה לֹא נִתְפָּרְשׁוּ שְׁמוֹתָן שֶׁל זְקֵנִים,
chunks.en: And why are the names of the elders not written?
chunks.st: But why were the names of these seventy Elders not specified?

chunks.en: It is to teach
chunks.st: Rather, this comes to teach

chunks.en: that every group of three that stood
chunks.st: that every set of three judges that stands as

chunks.en: as a Beis Din over Yisrael
chunks.st: a court over the Jewish people

chunks.he: הֲרֵי הוּא כְבֵית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל משֶׁה.
chunks.en: is like the Beis Din of Moshe."
chunks.st: has the same status as the court of Moses.
chunks.stMore: Since it is not revealed who sat on that court, apparently it is enough that they were official judges in a Jewish court. When Rabbi Yehoshua heard that even Rabbi Dosa ben Horkinas maintained that they must submit to Rabban Gamliel’s decision,

chunks.en: He took his stick and his money in his hand,
chunks.st: he took his staff and his money in his hand,

chunks.he: וְהָלַךְ לְיַבְנֶה אֵצֶל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּיוֹם
chunks.en: and went to Yavneh, to Rabban Gamliel, on the day
chunks.st: and went to Yavne to Rabban Gamliel on the day on

chunks.en: that was Yom Kippur by his own counting.
chunks.st: which Yom Kippur occurred according to his own calculation.

chunks.he: עָמַד רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּנְשָׁקוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ,
chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel stood up and kissed him on his head.
chunks.st: Upon seeing him, Rabban Gamliel stood up and kissed him on his head.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: He said to him:

chunks.en: "Come in peace,
chunks.st: Come in peace,

chunks.en: my teacher and my student!
chunks.st: my teacher and my student.

chunks.en: My teacher in wisdom,
chunks.st: You are my teacher in wisdom,
chunks.stMore: as Rabbi Yehoshua was wiser than anyone else in his generation,

chunks.en: and my student, because you accepted my words."
chunks.st: and you are my student, as you accepted my statement, despite your disagreement.
